title: … and … Pair phrases
description: Learn fixed word pairs that make everyday English more natural.
objectives: Keep fixed phrases in their usual order

source.title: Advanced Grammar & Vocabulary — Express Publishing
source.note: Lesson vocabulary, examples and written tasks follow the supplied pages. Definitions are condensed for readability; spacing and obvious scan errors are corrected. Hints, explanations and model answers are study aids, not a publisher answer key.

lessons.title: Fixed pairs: amounts, time and situations
lessons.body: The document presents fixed expressions with and. Learn the pair in its usual order and use the original examples to connect the expression to its meaning.

lessons.title: Fixed pairs: relationships and reactions
lessons.body: Some pairs form part of a longer expression. Keep the surrounding words too: make a song and dance about, part and parcel of, and your own flesh and blood.

lessons.title: Fixed pairs: condition, outcomes and fairness
lessons.body: The remaining phrases describe safety, cleanliness, uncertainty, promise, changes and outcomes. These are the phrases needed for the document’s completion, repair and rewriting tasks.

vocabulary.example: We're receiving food, but it is only arriving in dribs and drabs.

vocabulary.definition: Very early, with a positive sense of readiness.
vocabulary.example: If we leave bright and early tomorrow morning, we should get there by midday.
vocabulary.note: Often with leave, start or get up.

vocabulary.example: By and large, most people would prefer to have a badly paid job that they liked rather than a well paid job that they disliked.
Good jobs are few and far between in days of high unemployment.

vocabulary.definition: Accept an unpleasant situation without complaining.
vocabulary.example: A shorter lunch break is new company policy, so we'll just have to grin and bear it.

vocabulary.definition: The details of a complicated situation.
vocabulary.example: We have yet to discuss all the ins and outs of his proposal.
vocabulary.note: Usually the ins and outs of.

vocabulary.example: I was only 10 minutes late. Why are you making such a song and dance about it?
vocabulary.note: Usually make a song and dance about.

vocabulary.example: Everything had been packed away in boxes except for a few odds and ends.

vocabulary.definition: Finally and decisively, ending doubt or repetition.
vocabulary.example: He set out to prove once and for all that Deakin's alibi was nothing but a tissue of lies.
We're talking about my family here, my own flesh and blood. Of course I trust them.
That is an out-and-out lie; you've made it all up!
Having your private life splashed across the front pages of newspapers and glossy magazines is part and parcel of being a celebrity.
We took a couple of days off and went to the country for a bit of peace and quiet.
His car/daughter/garden is his pride and joy.

vocabulary.definition: Very formal, conventional and easily shocked.
vocabulary.example: She's far too prim and proper to have written anything as scandalous as that.
After a lot of pushing and shoving, I finally made it to the counter where everything had been reduced by 50%.

vocabulary.definition: Safe and unharmed after possible danger.
vocabulary.example: The two children, who had been missing for three days, were found safe and sound hiding in an abandoned mine shaft.
vocabulary.note: Often after arrive, return or be found.

vocabulary.example: When I get back, I want this place looking spick and span.
vocabulary.note: US variant spic and span is also used.

vocabulary.definition: Uncertain, especially for a serious outcome.
vocabulary.example: It was touch and go whether they would allow us to leave the country.
vocabulary.note: Often it was touch and go whether.

vocabulary.example: The government has introduced a scheme whereby up-and-coming young athletes will receive financial support.
What family doesn't have its ups and downs?
Even allowing for wear and tear, these chair covers should last for at least fifteen years.
After walking for three hours, we realised that we were well and truly lost. / As we had been well and truly beaten the Saturday before, the manager decided to make wholesale changes to the team.

vocabulary.definition: Honestly and according to the rules.
vocabulary.example: What do you mean I cheated? I won fair and square, and you know it.
